description: REQ-109's own EARS text defines default detection entirely in terms of `issued_ms`: 'WHEN a loan's due_ms (issued_ms + LOAN_REPAYMENT_WINDOW_DAYS * 86400000) has passed ...' (line 1412), and REQ-105's cold-start monitoring function orders loans 'by issued_ms ascending' (line 566, 583). Yet `issued_ms` is used a total of six times across this document (lines 540, 566, 581, 583, 1412, 1514) and is NEVER once defined -- no statement anywhere specifies which of REQ-106's own TWO ledger rows (the 'provisioning' row appended BEFORE payViaFacilitator is even attempted, or the 'active' follow-up row appended AFTER the transfer is confirmed, possibly after an arbitrarily-delayed crash/reconciliation recovery) carries this field, or at what wall-clock moment it is set. This is a materially different field from the two REQ-106 DOES explicitly name and define timing for: `provisioned_ms` (lines 777, 863, explicitly 'the provisional row's own provisioned_ms', used only as the starting point for reconcileProvisionalDisbursement's own block-range scan) is a DIFFERENT, separately-named field -- its existence and distinct name implies `issued_ms` is meant to be set at a DIFFERENT point (most plausibly, when the follow-up 'active' row is appended), but the spec never says so explicitly anywhere in REQ-106's own two-phase-append description (lines ~746-753) or REQ-104/105/109's own bodies. This ambiguity has real monetary consequences precisely in the crash-recovery scenario this spec has otherwise hardened so carefully (FIND-103/FIND-201/FIND-301): if `issued_ms` is set at PROVISIONAL-row time (before the transfer is even attempted) and a reconciliation is delayed by hours or days (e.g. a stuck facilitator, a slow-to-resolve RPC issue, or simply because -- per FIND-401's own finding -- reconciliation for a lender is only re-attempted 'at the START of the NEXT loan-issuance attempt for this SAME lender,' which could be arbitrarily far in the future), the borrower's `due_ms` clock (issued_ms + 14 days) would already be running down BEFORE the borrower ever actually received the funds or before the loan was ever confirmed 'active' -- silently shortening the borrower's real, usable 14-day repayment window and unfairly increasing default risk through no fault of the borrower. Conversely, if `issued_ms` is set at follow-up/'active'-row time, a loan whose real on-chain transfer landed days before reconciliation discovered it would get a FRESH 14-day window starting from the (much later) reconciliation moment, giving the borrower a materially LONGER usable window than a normally-issued loan of the same real disbursement date -- an inconsistency across loans that undergo normal-path vs. reconciled-path issuance. Neither behavior is stated as intended anywhere, and no Edge Case or Acceptance Criterion in REQ-106/104/109 addresses which applies. No PROP in verification-architecture.md's own reconciliation fixtures (PROP-106g/h/k/l) asserts what value `issued_ms` takes on a reconciled row, so an implementation could resolve this ambiguity either way and still pass every stated proof obligation.

evidence.snippet: WHEN a loan's due_ms (issued_ms + LOAN_REPAYMENT_WINDOW_DAYS * 86400000) has passed AND its last-appended row's repaid_usd is still less than total_due_usd ... [REQ-105] the first n (by issued_ms ascending, across ALL borrowers colony-wide) loans ...

crossCheck.note: REQ-106's own two-phase append description names the provisional row's timestamp field explicitly as `provisioned_ms` (a DIFFERENT field from issued_ms, used only for reconcileProvisionalDisbursement's own block-range scan start) -- confirming issued_ms is a distinct field whose own set-point (provisional-append time vs. follow-up-append time) is never once stated anywhere in this document.
